verdict.rationale: Superhuman documents automations that run in the background without user action: emails are labeled on arrival, user-written custom Auto Labels, toggleable Auto Archive, and auto-drafts with follow-up reminders. User-defined automation is limited to label prompts and on/off toggles. The trigger-based agent builder appears only on a general what's-new page and is not clearly tied to Mail, and MCP sends still require explicit approval. Missing for 10: clear evidence that users can author arbitrary trigger→action automations within Mail, documentation of the scope and limits of the agent builder, and independent or hands-on corroboration that these automations run reliably unattended.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: You can even make your own Auto Labels with short AI prompts like "job applications" or "requests to review work".
Turn on Auto Archive, and eliminate inbox clutter for good.
